version.approval_notes: Power Loader is an internal casework tool deployed by organisations through enterprise policy. Hosted demo with fictional pages and a forms library, plus a step-by-step guide: https://powerloader.surprisingly.ltd/try (in the sidebar's Settings, enter https://powerloader.surprisingly.ltd/demo/library/ and press Connect, then start a case and clip the demo pages). Full reviewer notes: https://powerloader.surprisingly.ltd/reviewers (permissions, CSP, no remote code, the privacy model download, and every vendored library file with its npm release and SHA-256, also shipped as vendor/SOURCES.tsv). To rebuild with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 11.3.0: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build:ext (see REVIEWERS.md). Our own code in extension/ is not minified. Privacy policy: https://powerloader.surprisingly.ltd/privacy AI is optional and off until configured: organisations can run with no AI (flows built by hand) or with their own OpenAI-compatible gateway, and policy can lock the gateway address, the privacy model, redaction and site rules. The text of every AI request is redacted on the computer (by default with the on-device privacy model) and sent only after the user approves a preview. A picture can be sent only from the reader’s Enhanced mode, unredacted, after the user ticks that they understand; policy redaction.blockImages prevents it. Requires Firefox 140+. No permanent host access; individual origins requested at runtime. Declares website content, personal, financial/payment and health data. Source archive includes build instructions and SOURCE.json. Transformers.js web entry is bundled with stable ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 using esbuild 0.27.2 to exclude its upstream prerelease runtime; vendor/BUNDLE.json records inputs. Other third-party files are unmodified npm releases. New in 1.1.0: the alarms permission (no prompt), for the hourly library sync and for deleting a case left unused for 24 hours; fetch steps, which request pages from the casework site the tab is on with GET only, read them as data and keep short text excerpts in the case (REVIEWERS.md, Fetch steps); and outlines drawn on pages in a closed shadow root. No new host permissions.

release_notes.en-US:
- Every case now starts from a flow. Pick one on the Case tab; star the ones you use and they come first.
- Two modes, switched at the top of the sidebar: Casework, for working a case, and Build, for making and mending flows. Build has a Templates tab with every page and form your flows use.
- A case's steps are listed in order and ticked when done. The open step has one main button: always the next thing to do.
- The values a page gives are outlined on the page and listed in the step, and they travel to the sidebar when you clip it.
- A step can have a condition: it is needed only when the case has, or lacks, a value. Otherwise Next passes over it.
- If you open a page that isn't in the flow, Power Loader asks whether the flow is missing it. You can add it in Build, and the open case can take the changed flow.
- Conflicts are orange, in the step and on the page. Each links to its card and to the pages its values came from, and the step's line updates as you go.
- A template can have a rule that opens a closed part of a page, such as an accordion, to show a value.
- Fetch steps read pages from the casework system you are on without opening them. They only read: nothing is posted. They can read JSON, and every link in a list on the page. While one runs, a box on the page shows each request, and the Fetched view shows what was read.
- Flows can also have steps to send an email or read a screenshot, and notes shown on a page.
- A flow can take the case reference from the case you open.
- Site rules (allow and deny) limit where Power Loader may read, fill, draw or fetch. Your organisation, your library or you can set them.
- A case is cleared when Firefox closes, and after 24 hours without use. You can change both in Settings unless your organisation has set them.
- Each tool (region capture, reader, calculator, timeline, notes on pages) has its own switch in Settings, which your organisation can set.
- The forms library syncs by itself, at start and every hour, and can carry flows.
- The on-device privacy model is on by default and can be switched off. It can come from a folder on any web server, with Test connection.
- Organisations can build their own version with a policy file built in.
- A new icon.
- Profile drafts made outside a flow are no longer used.
- For library teams: check where your flows' instructions say a button is. Clip this page is now in the open step.
